title: Stack Buffer Overflow in cURL Cookie Parsing Leads to RCE
classified_slop_by: Daniel Stenberg gist 07f7581f6e3d78ef37dfbfc81fd1d1cd (AI slop security reports submitted to curl)
why_rejected: Closed on HackerOne as not-applicable and listed as AI slop in Stenberg's gist. The claim is bogus: the only demonstration is a standalone test program that fills an 8192-byte local array with no null terminator and then calls strlen() on it — AddressSanitizer flags the reporter's own out-of-bounds read, not any code path in libcurl's cookie parser. curl bounds cookie length (CURL_MAX_HTTP_HEADER / per-cookie limits) and does not strlen() unterminated attacker data, so no overflow exists in curl. The report is explicitly fuzzing/AI-assisted narrative with no curl crash. The public disclosure JSON exposes no maintainer comment text.
note: report.md is the reporter's description with PoC source and raw AddressSanitizer output removed; it is framed as the reporter's claims.
